status: Available to foreigners with Chinese tax records
who: Not a mainland Chinese national; working or has worked in China; holds a Chinese tax record showing tax paid within the last 3 years. Personal accounts only.
limit: 300,000 CNY per transfer from a Chinese bank app; 50,000 CNY per transfer from Alipay. Overall limit is about the salary earned in China after Chinese tax, and it does not expire.
delivery: Only to another account in your own name: a bank account outside China or your Wise account.
advantages: Fully online after a one-time check (1 to 2 working days). Tax records are requested once, not for every transfer. The provider states its fee before you pay.
drawbacks: Only covers taxed salary; savings from other origins do not raise the limit. Fee and rate for CNY to USD were not read. The Chinese partner company is not named on the page.

channel: Western Union at a partner bank
status: Available on a passport; cash pickup
who: Sender shows a China ID card, a passport (not Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan passports) or a Mainland Travel Permit. Online sending is for residents of China through a partner bank's online banking.
delivery: Cash pickup at an agent location abroad. The page shows a banner that transfers to a bank account are temporarily unavailable.
advantages: Money is available in minutes. Works at Bank of China, China Everbright Bank, Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, Postal Savings Bank of China and five smaller banks. The United States is on Postal Savings Bank's list of 84 allowed destinations.
drawbacks: Someone must collect cash in the U.S. Fee and amount limits are not on the page. Partner banks restrict some countries and passport holders, and may require a bank account to send.
